Ava Lin: ran a short nsys trace against the kv-heavy replay workload, seeing a weird concentration of time in a kernel named `warpHeatKernel` and a CPU-side task `kv_cache_eviction`. attaching top-line numbers and timeline link.
Carlos Mendez: can you paste the nsys cmd + the top-kernel list? curious about batch/seq config.
Ava Lin: command was `nsys profile -o replay-kv -t cuda,kern,cudaMemory --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --force-overwrite --cuda-memory-usage=true --stats=true --trace-fork=true --delay=0 --app=./replay_runner`.
Ava Lin: batch=8, seq_len=1024, kv shards=4, kv cache ~6GB, quant=q4_0.
Ava Lin: top kernels by GPU time from the nsys summary:
```
warpHeatKernel            41.7%   1.82s
kv_prefetch_loader        9.3%    0.41s
attn_forward              12.4%   0.54s
kv_cache_eviction_kernel  18.1%   0.79s
softmax                   3.2%    0.14s
other                     15.3%   0.67s
```
Priya Rao: interesting that kv_cache_eviction shows as a kernel for you; on my traces eviction is mostly CPU work with a memcpy. do you see memcpy DtoH/HtoD spikes? or is eviction launching a GPU kernel?
Ava Lin: looks like eviction does a GPU kernel in our path: we call `evict_and_compact_kernel` after batch boundaries to compact the slab. nvtx markers show it aligns with the KV eviction stage.
eng-bot: perf alert: p95 latency +18% during trace window 2088887777 (trace id replay-kv). correlated with GPU busy time increase.
Carlos Mendez: do we have SM util / occupancy numbers around the warpHeatKernel period? could be divergence or low occupancy
Ava Lin: nvprof slice (sm metrics) around the hotspot: SM_efficiency ~ 28%, achieved_occupancy ~ 0.31, divergent_warp_ratio high (~0.44) during warpHeatKernel spikes.
Joon Park: low occupancy + high divergence => probably lots of branchy work per thread in that kernel. warpHeatKernel name suggests some per-warp reduction or histogram. Does the kernel iterate variable-length loops? also check register usage — high regs reduces occupancy.
Priya Rao: also consider that eviction kernel may be running on the critical path and creating KV backpressure. If eviction compacts memory, it might serialize and produce idle SM periods between batches — that would explain SM-eff low even though a kernel is consuming time.
Ava Lin: timeline screenshot: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/replay-kv/2088887777 (private). You can see compact kernel runs in bursts and immediately after we get a wave of attn_forward kernels with a long stall preceding them.
Carlos Mendez: hypothesis: continuous batching heuristic accumulates requests until N tokens then fires eviction->compact. If compact is heavy for certain sequence patterns (e.g., lots of long contexts) then GPU bursts align and cause contention. Maybe kernel selection picked a generic compact kernel rather than the 'compact_fast' variant.
Priya Rao: can you run a comparison with kernel override env to force `compact_fast` (lower regs, more parallel) vs `compact_stable`? even a microbenchmark with synthetic KV patterns should expose throughput delta.
Ava Lin: will try. also going to re-run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` for easier timeline correlation and a perf counter set including `sm__inst_executed.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active` and `tensor_core_utilization`.
Joon Park: when you run microbench, capture `/proc/interrupts` and `dmesg` too — we've seen occasional PCIe errors causing DtoH stalls that look like kernel hotspots.
Ava Lin: noted. plan: 1) microbench compact_fast vs compact_stable, 2) run a seq sweep (256/512/1024) to see scaling, 3) collect nvprof counters + nsys timeline with mem copies annotated, 4) if still high, instrument compact kernel for branch hist and regs via nvcc -lineinfo and `cuobjdump --dump-sass`.
Carlos Mendez: thanks. if compact_fast reduces reg pressure and occupancy improves, we can add selection rule in kernel selector: prefer low-reg variant when seq_len>512 and kv_shards>2.
Priya Rao: and add a telemetry event for eviction duration + post-evict first-token latency so we can automatic-alert when eviction exceeds X ms.
Ava Lin: will iterate. logging next steps here and ping when I have microbench results :thumbsup:
Carlos Mendez: :eye: keep an eye on `kv_prefetch_loader` too — it could be contributing with concurrent memory traffic.
eng-bot: reminder: create perf ticket if regression persists. ticket template: /tickets new perf "kv-evict-warpheat".
Ava Lin: created ticket PERF-4132 and linked trace. I'll post results in this thread.
